valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E. Earnings period priced at the Nov 2027 target date is FY2028 (year to Jan 2028), non-GAAP diluted EPS including stock compensation, on about 24.2B diluted shares, 17% tax. Q3 FY27 guide: revenue $108B, 74% gross margin, $9.0B opex implies about $70.9B operating income and EPS near $2.46. USD listing, no FX.

bear.driver: Data center digestion and supply or visibility problems in 2027 (Baird's thesis), gross margin near 70%, leadership transition and export limits keep multiple compressed

base.driver: Rubin ramp keeps revenue growing but below the Street, margin about 73-74%, buybacks offset dilution; EPS about 7% below the $15.5-15.75 consensus

bull.driver: Guide-and-beat cadence continues, FY2028 EPS matches or beats consensus and the CEO transition proves orderly, restoring a premium multiple

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $14.50 the $162.85 close implies 11.2x. The engine's only active 12-month-horizon target (Baird $200) implies 13.8x base EPS, or EPS $14.29 at 14x; the broader named-target set (Wedbush $275, Morgan Stanley $300, Oppenheimer $315, Goldman $300, Truist $346) implies roughly 19-24x base EPS.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $14.50 (8.9 pp of the close); $1 of EPS moves it by $14.
valuation.watch_metric: Data center revenue and Q4 FY27 revenue guidance versus the $108B Q3 guide, plus gross margin at or above 74% and commentary on Rubin timing and China
valuation.next_disclosure: Q3 FY2027 results, scheduled Nov 17, 2026 (after close; date per company notice, results not yet released as of Nov 16)

analyst_notes: Named calls before the Nov 13 close split into stale post-Q2 raises (Aug 27: Wedbush, Truist, Morgan Stanley, Oppenheimer, Goldman at $300-346) and sharp November resets (Wedbush $345 to $275, Baird $500 to $200 with a downgrade to Neutral). Only Baird's target documents a 12-month horizon, so the engine's weighted target rests on that single call ($200); the other targets have a null horizon and sit well above it. Many other cuts reported (HSBC Hold $170, Evercore, Rosenblatt, Bernstein, Craig-Hallum, BofA) lacked a named analyst or a verifiable pre-close time and are excluded, as are Nov 16 cuts (Barclays, TD Cowen, Mizuho) that postdate the reference close. Wedbush's $275 uses 17.5x FY2028 EPS of $15.53; my base EPS is about 7% below that, so the gap to the Street is mostly multiple.
